bug_semantics: PHProxy's intended SSRF control for user-supplied proxy targets is a hostname-string regex blacklist ($_hosts, default '#^127\.|192\.168\.|10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|localhost#i') applied with preg_match against parse_url() host only. Unauthenticated callers supply the target via the configured URL parameter (url_var_name; '_proxurl' in v1.1.1 and HEAD). A hostname that does not literally match those prefixes (PoC: a public DNS name such as vul.aegisrisk.xyz bound to 127.0.0.1) is allowed, after which the proxy opens a server-side HTTP(S) connection to the resolved internal address. That bypasses the blacklist and reaches loopback/RFC1918 services (CWE-918). CVE-2025-52362 / GHSA-37c4-9pw5-3r33 (published, not withdrawn) affect v1.1.1 and prior.
flaw_origin: The hostname-only $_hosts regex and the preg_match($_hosts, $_url_parts['host']) gate were first written in this repository by 74393b7dd065a0960e7d35d1a39f9862fcc3cc93 (2015-10-21, Miglen, 'Initial commit' of the SourceForge poxy/PHProxy 0.5 tree). Parent 0150ea6f802790d2b42ddb2e623ef4a4224aa0ca contains only .gitattributes/.gitignore; index.php and the regex are absent. No finer public git member exists. The same string-match (no DNS resolution, no IP-range check) is still the browser-flow gate at HEAD. 08eb632aa59e076645d2a115112976e3891a20b9 is a 2018 restore after an accidental wipe, not a first write. 2026 Claude-coauthored 'SSRF guard' copies (bd7f6dd, 036e825) reuse the same hostname regex for new APIs and do not close the DNS bypass.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-52362 is a published MITRE record (not withdrawn/rejected) for SSRF in PHProxy <=1.1.1. The mechanism is not 'the proxy fetches URLs' in the abstract; the project already tried to block private targets, but the check is preg_match on the hostname string. A public name that resolves to 127.0.0.1/RFC1918 therefore drives a server-side fetch of internal services via _proxurl (or the older q parameter). BIC search used git log -S / parent-tree absence, not an AI-commit hunt. 74393b7dd065a0960e7d35d1a39f9862fcc3cc93 is the first commit whose tree contains $_hosts and the preg_match gate; its parent 0150ea6f802790d2b42ddb2e623ef4a4224aa0ca was checked directly and lacks index.php. 08eb632 is a revert/restore after biojet1/Phoenix wiped index.php and is not a first write. 84cb6ee/c702330 only restyle or inline the same check. AI is judged only on the BIC object: 2015 human import of 2004-2007 PHProxy, no AI trailers. 2026 Claude-coauthored API guards copied the broken regex and must not be treated as BIC or as a fix. Cross-check: BIC precedes v1.1.1; no patched boundary exists because HEAD/v1.3.3 still match host strings only. Verdict NOT_AI with an explicit unpatched record.

unpatched.reason: HEAD index.php still blacklists only hostname strings via $_hosts preg_match (lines 716-718, 1722-1728). The 2026 'SSRF guard' (bd7f6dd) and phproxy_api_validate_host (036e825) copy that same regex for new APIs and still do not resolve DNS. git log v1.1.1..HEAD -S 'preg_match($host, $_url_parts' is empty. GitHub has no SSRF/CVE-2025-52362 issue or PR. v1.3.3 therefore does not close the advisory.

potential_fix.approach: After parsing the target URL, resolve the host to all A/AAAA records, pin the outbound socket to those IPs, and reject the request if any address is loopback, RFC1918, link-local (including 169.254.169.254), CGNAT 100.64/10, RFC2544, IPv6 ::1/ULA/mapped, or other reserved ranges; re-validate after every redirect; restrict schemes to http/https. Apply the same resolved-IP check in the browser _proxurl flow and in ?api=fetch/portcheck/dns/cert.
potential_fix.rationale: The disclosed bypass is that a non-matching hostname can still resolve to a blocked address. Checking and pinning resolved IPs closes that hole; hostname-regex replication cannot.
